page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 1890 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ds_v7 demonstrates strong CPU capabilities, particularly in single-threaded operations. It achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core performance with a score of 2232.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 36.5 GB/sec. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with a Passmark CPU score of 54563.93 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 18166.0. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block cached speed of 2684.62 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds reach 166.74 GB/sec and 65.26 GB/sec, respectively. The processor's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, aids in accelerating cryptographic and vector-based workloads.

This server configuration is highly suited for workloads requiring a balance of compute power, memory, and fast local storage. Appropriate use cases include relational databases, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale text or image processing. The inclusion of a generous 1890 GB local disk alongside dedicated CPU resources offers strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive applications that benefit from high-speed local scratch space without requiring expensive GPU acceleration.
